{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVrXwhM8AAAABeiFufw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BrPg-zhIDHfM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BrPg-", "number": 7, "title": "Add drag-to-orbit camera controls to the Neural Shadow demo", "body": "## Problem

The [Neural Shadow demo](https://github.com/takahirox/three-nn/blob/main/shadow.html) introduced by #5 currently uses a fixed `OrthographicCamera` in `src/shadow-demo.js`; the only spatial interaction is the **Light azimuth** slider. This makes it difficult to inspect the cast-shadow geometry, observe the same neural shadows from different viewpoints, and diagnose differences between Reference and Neural.

The model already predicts ground-plane shadow visibility from world-space ground position and light direction. **Camera pose is not a model input**, so adding view controls should **not require retraining the neural network**.

## Expected outcome and scope

Enable familiar, direct manipulation of the camera **inside the existing Neural Shadow canvas** using Three.js's `OrbitControls`:

- **Pointer/mouse drag:** orbit the camera around the fixed scene, horizontally through a full turn and vertically from useful elevated angles.
- **Mouse wheel / trackpad zoom and touch pinch:** zoom in/out at bounded levels. Use orthographic zoom with the existing `OrthographicCamera`; switching to `PerspectiveCamera` is not required.
- **Touch drag:** one-finger orbit on devices/browsers that support WebGPU and pointer/touch events.
- **Keep Light azimuth slider:** this continues to control light direction, *not* the camera. Camera orbit must not affect the light or the model inputs.
- **Keep Reference / Neural / Difference selection:** all modes use the **same live camera pose**; changing mode must never reset the camera. Difference must continue comparing the two techniques at identical camera/light/scene settings.
- **Provide a small 'Reset view' control** restoring the initial documented camera position, target and zoom (from `src/shadow-scene.json`); do not reset the light or view mode.
- Add a short visible hint near the canvas, e.g. "Drag to orbit · Scroll/pinch to zoom"; do not obstruct the rendered scene.

Limit camera behavior to orbit and zoom in this issue. **Disable panning**, maintain a stable orbit target (the current `spec.camera.target`), constrain polar angle to stay above the floor (for example 0.1 to `Math.PI/2 - 0.05` radians), and bound `minZoom`/`maxZoom` to prevent losing the scene or extreme clipping. Prefer simple, immediate controls (`enableDamping=false`) to preserve the existing render-on-demand design. Choose and document sensible limits.

### Integration with current code

Current relevant files:
- `src/shadow-demo.js`: creates the orthographic camera with `spec.camera.position` / `spec.camera.target`, renders only on interactions and resize, and exposes `window.shadowDemo.benchmark()` and `diagnostics()`.
- `src/shadow-scene.json`: holds the initial camera position/target and orthographic extent.
- `shadow.html`: contains canvas, mode selector, light azimuth slider, benchmark button and status.
- `src/style.css`: shared canvas and control styles.

Recommended implementation:
1. Import `OrbitControls` from `three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js` (use the already installed Three.js dependency).
2. Instantiate with `new OrbitControls(camera, canvas)` after configuring camera; explicitly set `controls.target` from `spec.camera.target` and call `controls.update()`. Use `controls.enablePan = false` and bounded `minPolarAngle`, `maxPolarAngle`, `minZoom`, `maxZoom`.
3. Listen for `controls` `change` and render the current selected mode. Do **not** add a permanent animation loop or recompile shaders on each camera change. Avoid duplicate renders when resetting the camera if practical.
4. Make canvas touch interaction intentional (for example `touch-action: none` on this canvas), without blocking touch/scroll interactions elsewhere on the page. Keep controls attached only to the canvas.
5. Preserve existing `resize()` aspect/orthographic-frustum logic, retaining camera `zoom` and current orbit/target across resizes (do not reinitialize controls/pose during resize).
6. When WebGPU initialization fails or the device is lost, leave controls unusable and avoid throwing from subsequent pointer events. Reuse existing visible error handling and clean up controls/listeners if appropriate.
7. When implementing **Reset view**, restore the scene-spec initial camera pose and zoom, with suitable button disabled state during initialization/failure/measurement.

### Benchmark correctness (important)

The current isolated benchmark disables the light and mode UI, but not camera input. Camera changes *during* a measurement would invalidate comparisons.

- **Disable OrbitControls and Reset view while measuring**; keep the active camera pose and current zoom **fixed throughout all warmup and sample frames**. Re-enable on completion or recoverable failure.
- Do not auto-reset camera when measurement starts or finishes: preserve the user-selected pose.
- Include `cameraPosition`, `cameraTarget` and `cameraZoom` in the benchmark result so Reference and Neural measurements can be compared at an identical view; if results from different camera poses are compared, clearly distinguish them.
- Keep existing timestamp-query / CPU measurement semantics. Do not add background renders or control-event renders that contaminate the isolated benchmark.
- Do not change model training, JSON weights, teacher data, shadow-map setup, light conventions, frame timing methodology or existing numerical accuracy tests.

### Technical boundaries

This is an **interaction/inspection improvement**, not a request for free-camera translation, fly controls, movable shadow casters, new light types, changing neural inputs, new training datasets, GI, or a speedup guarantee. No new GUI/control library is needed beyond the existing Three.js addon.

## Context and reproduction

On the current `shadow.html` demo:
1. Load in a supported WebGPU browser.
2. Drag inside the scene canvas or scroll over it.
3. Actual: no camera rotation/zoom (camera fixed); only moving the Light azimuth slider changes lighting.
4. Expected: canvas drag rotates the view and scroll/pinch zooms without changing the light or model weights.

Related: #5 (Neural Shadow implementation), #3 (original neural shading example).

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **AC1 — Orbit interaction:** dragging inside the Neural Shadow canvas orbits the existing orthographic camera about its fixed target; multiple azimuth and elevated viewpoints are reachable. Dragging outside the canvas does not move the camera. Pan is disabled and the camera cannot pass below the floor.
- [ ] **AC2 — Zoom and touch:** wheel/trackpad zoom works with documented bounds; one-finger touch orbit and two-finger pinch zoom work on a supported touch+WebGPU device, or the exact unsupported scenario and reason are reported as **Not run** (manual touch-device evidence is required when such a device is available; never report an untested path as Pass).
- [ ] **AC3 — Independent light/mode behavior:** camera movements do not change light azimuth; the Light azimuth slider continues working at an arbitrary camera pose. Reference, Neural and Difference all display the same pose, and mode switching preserves it without retraining.
- [ ] **AC4 — Reset and resize:** Reset view restores initial scene-spec camera position/target/zoom without resetting light/mode. Resizing retains the current camera pose and zoom and produces a correctly framed, undistorted canvas.
- [ ] **AC5 — Benchmark isolation:** during `window.shadowDemo.benchmark()` (including warmup), camera interaction and Reset view are disabled, pose/zoom stay constant, and no extra OrbitControls-triggered renders occur; controls are restored afterward when the demo remains healthy. Result JSON records camera position, target and zoom. Existing Reference-vs-Neural isolated measurements still work.
- [ ] **AC6 — No regression:** existing neural shadow model/shadow-map inference and Difference view remain correct; original `x^4` example still works; WebGPU-only validation and failure handling remain intact. No model retraining or new neural weights.
- [ ] **AC7 — Lightweight validation and docs:** `npm test` and `npm run build` pass; run an actual WebGPU browser smoke test covering orbit, zoom, reset, mode, light, resize and benchmark interactions. Update `README.md` and the on-page help with precise controls/limits. Report commands, relevant commit SHA, browser/OS/device and **Pass/Fail/Skipped/Not run** evidence on the PR according to repository policy.

## Validation already performed

**Not run:** implementation and browser behavior have not been changed or tested for this Issue yet. The existing demo source files and controls were inspected to formulate the requirements. Complete validation must target the eventual PR head.

## Optional validation

- A short screen recording of orbit + mode switching.
- Verify wheel and trackpad behavior on multiple browsers.
- Confirm benchmark view parameters remain identical across successive Reference and Neural runs.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Contributor guidance

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/three-nn/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/three-nn/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review/merge guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/three-nn/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), [UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/three-nn/blob/main/docs/ui-ux-principles.md), and [testing/CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/three-nn/blob/main/docs/testing-ci-principles.md). Keep the change focused and link PR evidence to the stable AC identifiers. Repository collaboration text should be in English.
